source_citation: Ecological and morphological study of Mimosa depauperata, M. lacerata, M. similis and Mimosa texana var. texana from the Estórax River Basin, Querétaro, Mexico; taxonomic description pp. 44–45 as extracted from institutional PDF
source_name: Mimosa texana (A.Gray) Small and Mimosa texana var. texana

morphology_source_reported.species_habit: Shrub usually 30 cm–2 m tall or small tree 2–3 m
morphology_source_reported.species_young_branches: Reddish, ridged/striated, puberulent, with resinous dots
morphology_source_reported.spines: Recurved infra-stipular prickles, commonly solitary but occasionally paired or 3 together
morphology_source_reported.leaves: 1–6 pairs of pinnae and 3–10 pairs of leaflets per pinna (species-wide); leaflets oblique linear/oblong to elliptic 1.5–4 × 0.5–2 mm
morphology_source_reported.flower_heads: Globose 0.8–1.5 cm wide, axillary solitary or 2–5 together
morphology_source_reported.corolla: Pink-purple 2.2–4 mm, five-lobed; lobes free for 1/5–1/3 of corolla length
morphology_source_reported.stamens: Usually 10, rarely 9, free filaments white to lilac
morphology_source_reported.fruit_species: Linear to oblong pod 1.8–4.5 cm long and 4–7 mm wide; straight to curved, valves intact, spiny to unarmed margins
morphology_source_reported.var_texana_distinction: Usually shrub 15–75 cm tall; 1–3 pinna pairs, 4–7 leaflet pairs; solitary mostly recurved prickles; 2.5–3.2 cm pods; original varietal fruit width appears 0.5–0.7 mm inconsistent with species account, therefore withheld

taxonomic_scope: Species range includes variation not wholly characteristic of Texas var. texana; populations in queried Mexican study were var. texana.
